title: Health-worker sit-in for unpaid Covid bonuses reported retrospectively
threshold_50_evidence: No public gathering attendance estimate established.

start_date.summary: June report locates an actual prior sit-in in January 2021; no day supplied.

location.summary: January site not specified; June Abidjan context cannot prove precise January location.

demands.summary: Unpaid government Covid bonuses and appeal to budget minister.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No January attendance; December beneficiaries cannot be converted into crowd size.

state_response.summary: December and June official/police behavior is outside January; seven January responses remain unknown.

notes.summary: Possible cross-month dispute linkage only; no automatic continuous event.

notes: June AIP reporting explicitly recalls a January 2021 sit-in addressed to the budget minister. Doctors, pharmacists, dentists, nurses, midwives and technicians are described. December 18 protest may concern overlapping actors and demands; continuity is unresolved. December reception and June proposed audience/police presence are not January responses.
open_questions: Was attendance at least 50 and was this one or several January assemblies?
Was January a new physical episode after the December 18 action?
What were the January day, precise site, organizer, physical closure and state responses?

title: Bouaké university union assembly launching an indefinite strike
threshold_50_evidence: No public gathering attendance estimate established.

start_date.summary: January 14 article explicitly dates actual first general assembly to January 5.

location.summary: University in Bouaké; January 13 assembly identified campus 1, which is not automatically January 5 site.

organizer.summary: Intersyndicale named SYNARES, CNEC and PAT.

demands.summary: Student reintegration and orientation commission are education governance demands; no staff wage demand reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Assembly reported without attendance. Student placement totals measure affected people.

end_date.summary: January 13 suspension is organizational decision, not reported physical closure.

state_response.summary: Minister's promise reported without actual meeting/reception proof; all seven responses unknown.

notes: January 14 retrospective contemporary report confirms January 5 general assembly launching strike. Undated InfoIvoire announcement independently describes a planned January 5 assembly but cannot establish occurrence itself. Demand: reintegrate excluded 2019 students and restore national orientation commission. January 13 assembly suspended strike after minister's promise; suspension does not establish physical closure. Roughly 2,000 or 3,000 affected students in respective reports are not attendees. Ministerial promise alone is not coded accommodation.
open_questions: Was January 5 assembly public and attended by at least 50?
Was January 13 a distinct assembly or part of one physical episode?
Was there actual official negotiation/reception and when did any physical assembly end?

title: Cocoa producer strike over blocked marketing and government arrears
scope: national strike dispute; public assembly scope unknown
threshold_50_evidence: No public gathering attendance estimate established.

demands.summary: Government-linked cocoa marketing, producer remuneration arrears and regulator support.

start_date.summary: Planned and then reported January 18 work stoppage; no demonstrated public assembly onset, left null.

location.summary: National dispute, subsequent Daloa meeting mentioned without sufficient episode detail.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No number or clear >=50 description of a public gathering.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Actual consultations with Agriculture Minister Kobenan Kouassi Adjoumani support accommodation for the dispute; does not establish qualifying public assembly.

end_date.summary: January 21 call withdrawal and later Daloa call to end are not physical closure evidence.

notes: January 14 announcement proposed January 18 strike. January 22 report says strike did start January 18 and reports actual ministerial consultations and January 21 strike-call withdrawal. These establish industrial action and negotiation, not a public gathering of 50. Public assembly onset remains null. State demands concern blocked cocoa marketing, government arrears from 2016–17 and regulator support/assets. February 2 Daloa article appears to discuss this dispute; no automatic separate city record or physical end inferred from call-off.
open_questions: Was any qualifying public assembly held during the strike, where and when?
What was assembly attendance and its physical closure?
How does Daloa follow-up relate to the national call-off?

title: Bouaké lycée students oppose police arrest; protest versus gang interference unresolved
threshold_50_evidence: No public gathering attendance estimate established.

start_date.summary: February 2 reporting says last Thursday, corresponding to January 28; principal interview introduction has contradictory January date typo.

organizer.summary: Students, reportedly companions of accused boy; organized protest not established.

demands.summary: Opposition to police arrest implies objection to policing action, but qualifying demand remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: Anonymous student account says companions attacked police; attributed reporting, not independent verification.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No opposition crowd estimate; school enrollment and class sizes are irrelevant.

state_response.summary: Police arrest of boy precedes/motivates opposition, not response to it; seven responses unknown.

notes: February 2 report describes preceding Thursday students opposing police arrest of a boy accused of knife attack, including attacks on police. January 28 inferred from that weekday context. This may be interference by alleged gang members rather than qualifying public protest; target/assembly/threshold require review. The boy's arrest motivated opposition and is not coded current protest arrests. Subsequent rival-student fight is not automatically the same protest. Teachers' security strike began February 1 and belongs to neighboring month. Same outlet interview is additional detail, not independent corroboration.
open_questions: Was this a public political assembly rather than criminal/gang interference?
How many participants opposed police and what explicit state demand was made?
Was the inferred January 28 date correct and were there current protest responses?

title: Retrospective claim of teacher strike connected to January salary suspension
threshold_50_evidence: No public gathering attendance estimate established.

notes.summary: Retrospective salary-sanction claim; issue heading August 15–31, 2022.

start_date.summary: January sanction date cannot establish strike/public assembly onset, hence null.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: 300 sanctioned workers are not public attendance.

notes: August 2022 political bulletin claims 300 teachers had salary suspended in January 2021 after a three-day strike. January dates the salary sanction, not necessarily the strike. No public assembly, strike onset, demand, organizer or state target is established. No January occurrence asserted; retained research lead only. The 300 sanctioned teachers are not a crowd count. Pay suspension is not automatically any of seven coded state responses.
open_questions: When did strike occur and was there a qualifying January assembly?
What were state-directed demands, organizers, location and actual attendance?
Can contemporaneous independent reporting confirm the retrospective claim?

title: Adiaké students disrupt classes; demand and assembly unknown
threshold_50_evidence: No public gathering attendance estimate established.

start_date.summary: Disruption January 4 reported; no public assembly onset established.

notes.summary: Principal met students and parents; classes resumed January 5; no demand or attendance.

notes: Body reports January 4 class disruption and January 5 resumption after principal met students/parents. No reported demands, public gathering, crowd size or state-policy target. January 4 is action date only; public assembly onset remains null. School principal meeting does not alone establish state accommodation. Publication date not identified in article body.
open_questions: What motivated January 4 disruption and was it public assembly?
Did at least 50 participate and was a domestic state-policy demand made?
Was principal an acting state authority receiving policy demands or ordinary school mediation?
